source: Harris 3e Tables 32.1 to 32.8, PDF pages 750-757 (printed pp. 32.8-32.15)
about:
Forty-eight rows over the eight tables of Chapter 32, "Aislamiento del sonido transmitido por estructuras", of the Spanish edition: forty-two floor-ceiling constructions with the impact insulation class measured on them (Tables 32.1 to 32.7) and six elastic surface treatments with the improvement each one adds over a hard massive floor (Table 32.8).

The IIC is a single-number rating and these pages print no frequency band at all. There is no column of impact sound pressure levels here, nothing per octave or per third octave, and no reference curve: a caller after a band-by-band impact level will not find one in this catalogue.

The running text on folio 32.7 (PDF page 749) introduces the seven tables of constructions and says the data are "datos de mediciones del aislamiento del ruido de impacto" based on the chapter's Reference 5, "A guide to airborne, impact and structureborne noise control in multi-family dwellings", prepared for the Federal Housing Administration by the National Bureau of Standards, September 1967. Table 32.8 is presented apart, on folio 32.15, and carries its own credit line, "Fuente: Referencia 6.", which is W. Zeller, Laermbekaempfung, vol 7, 1963, p. 21. So these are collected measurements, not a calculation and not a specification; the page names no laboratory, no test standard and no uncertainty for any row. Each row carries the credit that covers its table in attributed_to, because the two credits are different and a row read on its own would otherwise answer the same source for a 1967 American survey and a 1963 German paper.

The rows are numbered 1 to 38 straight through the first seven tables, with a letter where a construction is printed as two lettered rows (34A, 34B, 35A, 35B, 36A, 36B, 37A, 37B), each with a description and a rating of its own, which is why none of them is held as a variant of the other, and that printed number is the key of the row here. Table 32.8 numbers no row, so those six are keyed by a slug of the printed treatment. Twelve of the descriptions are printed in full and refer to another row rather than repeating the structural floor ("Igual que 1 salvo que...", "Mismo suelo estructural que el 18"); the printed text is kept whole and the row it points at is recorded in refers_to_row. Three of those twelve print "Parecido al anterior" with no number, and for them the row referred to follows from the position on the page rather than from anything printed, which is why they say so in carried.

Each row of the first seven tables also has an "Esquema" cell, which is a line drawing of the section and has no textual equivalent whatever. It is not a data column: the row records that the drawing is there and nothing else. The four rows that only refer to another one carry no drawing.

Two cells print no rating at all: row 30 of Table 32.5 and row 38 of Table 32.7. The page prints no dash and no convention for the gap, it is simply empty, so nothing fills it here, and each of the two rows says on its own note that the column is printed for it and its cell in it is blank. One cell of Table 32.8 prints an interval, "25 a 30", with the word "a" and not a dash, and is held as a range with no value.

Everything printed is already SI with the imperial equivalent in parentheses, so no cell of this catalogue was converted by this library. The descriptions are kept exactly as the page sets them, decimal commas and all, including the nineteen pairs whose two halves are not each other at the precision they are printed to: row 9 prints "30,8 cm (16 in)" where 16 in is 40,64 cm and every other 16 in of these eight tables is printed as 40,6 cm, row 31 prints "10,1 cm (2 in)" where 2 in is 5,08 cm, and row 38 prints "1,99 kg/m2 (44 oz/yd2)" where 44 oz/yd2 is 1,49 kg/m2. They are the page's own and this catalogue does not correct them: all three hundred and twenty pairs of the eight tables were converted and checked, the nineteen that fail are registered as one entry in docs/ERRATA.md, and the seventeen rows that carry one hold the printed description whole with the cell marked misprinted beside it. The mass densities the prose buries are lifted into a field of their own while the prose stays whole; two of the three are served, and row 35A's is not, because its two printed halves, 410 kg/m3 and 26,1 lb/ft3, are 2 per cent apart and the page does not say which one is the board.

The transcription was made twice, from the rendered pages, by two readers who never saw each other's work. Fifty-five cells differed. Thirty-eight of them were the filler text the two readers invented for a cell that is a drawing and prints nothing, and twelve were about whether a description that refers to another row counts as printed or as inherited; neither was a disagreement about the page. The five that were are settled cell by cell on the rendered page at up to six times: two fraction glyphs whose small 8 degrades to a k in this copy, and three decimal marks that the page sets as commas everywhere, including inside the imperial parentheses.
